name: GO Classes Test Series 2023 | NIELIT Mock Test 4

question.text:
Insert the missing number to complete the series
$$0,\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ , 8,15,24,35,48$$

  1. $2$
  2. $3$
  3. $4$
  4. $5$

Ajay can do a piece of work in $25$ days and Kunal can do it in $20$ days. They work for $5$ days and then Ajay goes away. In how many more days will Kunal finish the work?

  1. $10$ days
  2. $12$ days
  3. $14$ days
  4. None of these

Find the odd one:

  1. $441$
  2. $289$
  3. $361$
  4. $343$

Find the odd one among the following.

  1. $\text{SORE}$
  2. $\text{SOTLU}$
  3. $\text{NORGAE}$
  4. $\text{MEJNIAS}$

A man has $9$ friends ($4$ boys and $5$ girls). In how many ways can he invite them, if there have to be exactly $3$ girls in the invites?

  1. $10$
  2. $100$
  3. $160$
  4. None of these

A vessel contains $40$ litres of milk; the milkman delivers $10$ litres to the first house, and adds an equal quantity of water. He does exactly the same at the $2^{\text {nd }}$ and $3^{\text {rd }}$ houses. What is the ratio of milk and water when he has finished delivering at the third house?

  1. $27: 37$
  2. $26: 38$
  3. $27: 64$
  4. Data inadequate

At what angle the hands of a clock are inclined at $15$ minutes past $5?$

  1. $67 \dfrac 1  2^{\circ}$
  2. $62 \dfrac 1  2^{\circ}$
  3. $70^{\circ}$
  4. $63 \dfrac 3  4^{\circ}$

Find the number of zeros at the end of $100!$

  1. $24$
  2. $28$
  3. $26$
  4. None of these

My mother’s sister’s son’s father’s mother-in-law is related to me as
 

  1. Mother
     
  2. Grandmother
     
  3. Mother-in-law
     
  4. Aunt

A motorboat whose speed in still water is $10 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$ went $91 \mathrm{~km}$ downstream and then returned to its starting point. Calculate the speed of the river flow if the round trip took $20$ hours.

  1. $3 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$
  2. $4 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$
  3. $2 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$
  4. $8 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$

A girl leaves from her home. She first walks $30$ meters in the North-west direction and then $30 \mathrm{~m}$ in the South-West direction. Next, she walks $30$ meters in South-east direction. Finally, she turns towards her house. In which direction is she moving?

  1. North-east
  2. North-west
  3. South-east
  4. South-west

A rectangular tank is $30\mathrm{~m}$ long $20\mathrm{~m}$ broad. Water is being flown into it through a square pipe of side $5 \mathrm{~cm}$. What is the speed of water if the level of water in the tank rises by $1 \mathrm{~m}$ in $8$ hours?

  1. $30 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$
  2. $40 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$
  3. $36 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$
  4. None of these

A reduction of $10 \%$ in the price of sugar enables a housewife to buy $6.2 \mathrm{~kg}$ more for Rs.  $279.$ Find the reduced price per kilogram.

  1. Rs. $5$
  2. Rs. $4.5$
  3. Rs. $4.05$
  4. None of these

Read the following information carefully and answer the question below it.

Sejal is very found of collecting greeting cards. Her collection of $211$ cards has a good mix of Birthday cards, New year cards, Diwali cards, Christmas cards and even a Marriage Anniversary card. The number of Birthday cards is equal to the sum of all other except the Marriage Anniversary card. The number of New Year card is double of Diwali cards which in turn is double of Christmas cards.

The number of Christmas cards are:

  1. $10$
  2. $15$
  3. $20$
  4. $25$

$2 \log _{10} x-\log _x 0.01=f(x)$. Find the value of $f(0.1)$

  1. $-2$
  2. $0$
  3. $-4$
  4. $1$

If $x>1, y>1, z>1$ are three numbers in GP, then $\dfrac{1}{1+\log x}, \dfrac{1}{1+\log y}, \dfrac{1}{1+\log z}$ are in

  1. AP
  2. HP
  3. GP
  4. None of these

Read the following information carefully and answer the question below it.

Sejal is very found of collecting greeting cards. Her collection of $211$ cards has a good mix of Birthday cards, New year cards,Diwali cards, Christmas cards and even a Marriage Anniversary card. The number of Birthday cards is equal to the sum of all other except the Marriage Anniversary card. The number of New Year card is double of Diwali cards which in turn is double of Christmas cards.

The number of Diwali cards are:

  1. $25$
  2. $30$
  3. $35$
  4. $40$

Six years ago, the ratio of the ages of Kunal and Sagar was $6: 5,$ Four years hence, the ratio of their ages will be $11: 10$. What is Sagar's age at present (years)?

  1. $10$
  2. $12$
  3. $16$
  4. $14$

If the number $3402$ is converted from base $10$ to base $x$ it becomes $12630.$ Similarly, if the number $1579$ is converted from base $10$ to base $x$ it becomes $4414.$ What is the value of $x?$

  1. $7$
  2. $5$
  3. $8$
  4. $4$

Correct the following sentence.

  1. No sooner had I reached the office when I got the news of your arrival
  2. No sooner I had reached the office than I got the news of your arrival
  3. No sooner had I reached the office than I got the new of your arrival
  4. No sooner had I reached the office than I had got the new of your arrival

$\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}$ and $\mathrm{C}$ are employed to do a piece of work for Rs. $575. \;\text{A}$ and $\text{C}$ are supposed to finish $ \frac {17} {23}$ of the work together. Amount shall be paid to $\text{B}$ (in Rs) is ________.

  1. $150$
  2. $200$
  3. $225$
  4. $425$

Fill in the blank with an appropriate word phrase.

We were ________  in the middle of our conversation.

  1. cut out
  2. cut off
  3. cut up
  4. cut through

A sum of money doubles itself in $5$ years. In how many years will it become four fold (if interest is compounded)?

  1. $15$
  2. $10$
  3. $20$
  4. $12$

In an election there are $4$ parties. Elections are held for some number of assembly seats. Party $A$ lost $28$ seats, $B$ lost $24, C$ lost $31, D$ lost $22$ seats respectively.

The minimum seats won by any party are

  1. $4$
  2. $5$
  3. $6$
  4. None of these

In an election, there are $4$ parties. Elections are held for some number of assembly seats. Party $A$ lost $28$ seats, $B$ lost $24, C$ lost $31, D$ lost $22$ seats respectively.

Maximum seats won by any party are

  1. $15$
  2. $13$
  3. $12$
  4. None of these

$\text{A}$ starts business with Rs.$3500$ and $5$ months after $\text{B}$ joins $\text{A}$ as his partner. After a year the profits are divided in the ratio of $2: 3$. How much did $\text{B}$ contribute?

  1. Rs. $7000$
  2. Rs. $11000$
  3. Rs. $9000$
  4. None of these

$20$ litres of a mixture contains milk $\&$ water in the ratio of $5: 3$. If $4$ litres of this mixture is replaced by $4$ litres of milk, the ratio of milk to water in the new mixture would be ________.

  1. $2: 1$
  2. $7: 3$
  3. $8: 3$
  4. $4: 3$

The sum of the ages of $5$ children born at the intervals of $3$ years each is $50$ years. What is the age of the youngest child?

  1. $4$ years
  2. $8$ years
  3. $10$ years
  4. None of these

The average of the first $100$ positive integers is ______.

  1. $100$
  2. $51$
  3. $50.5$
  4. $49.5$

Mr. Kapur purchased two toy cycles for Rs. $750$ each. He sold these cycles, gaining $6 \%$ on one and losing $4 \%$ on the other. The gain or loss percent in the whole transaction is ______.

  1. $1 \%$ loss
  2. $2 \%$ gain
  3. $1.5 \%$ loss
  4. $1 \%$ gain

The compound interest on Rs. $8000$ at $20 \%$ per annum for $9$ months compounded quarterly is _______.

  1. $1261$
  2. $1250$
  3. $1270$
  4. $1258$

Read the following information carefully and answer the question below it.

Sejal is very found of collecting greeting cards. Her collection of $211$ cards has a good mix of Birthday cards, New year cards,Diwali cards, Christmas cards and even a Marriage Anniversary card. The number of Birthday cards is equal to the sum of all other except the Marriage Anniversary card. The number of New Year card is double of Diwali cards which in turn is double of Christmas cards.

The number of birthday cards in the collection is:

  1. $85$
  2. $95$
  3. $105$
  4. $110$

In an election, there are $4$ parties. Elections are held for some number of assembly seats. Party $A$ lost $28$ seats, $B$ lost $24, C$ lost $31, D$ lost $22$ seats respectively.

Find the total number of seats in the assembly.

  1. $45$
  2. $30$
  3. $35$
  4. $40$

The radius of the wheel of a vehicle is $70 \mathrm{~cm}$. The wheel makes $10$ revolutions in $5$ seconds. The speed of the vehicle is ________.

  1. $29.46 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$
  2. $31.68 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$
  3. $36.25 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$
  4. $32.72 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$

An observer $1.5\mathrm{~m}$ tall is $28.5 \mathrm{~m}$ away from a chimney. The angle of elevation of the top of the chimney from her eyes is $45^{\circ}$. What is the height of the chimney?

  1. $5$m
  2. $10$m
  3. $20$m
  4. $30$m

A train takes $10$ seconds to cross a man standing on a platform and $44$ seconds to cross the platform. What is the length of the platform if the speed of the train is $72 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}?$

  1. $440 \mathrm{~m}$
  2. $570 \mathrm{~m}$
  3. $680 \mathrm{~m}$
  4. None of these

In a polygon, the number of diagonals are $170$. The number of sides of the polygon are ______.
  1. $16$
  2. $20$
  3. $24$
  4. $34$

Rearrange the given set of statements in the right sequence.

  1. When one considers our distant, pre-human ancestors, answers begin to take shape.
  2. We need a restful sleep – would it not be more beneficial if the brain went totally ‘comatose’ until that rest was achieved? 
  3. But why would our brains enter into such a mixed state, representative of neither wakefulness nor sleeping? 
  4. For aeons, the safety provided by the spot where our predecessors chose to lay their heads for the night was, in many ways, compromised compared with the safety of our current bedroom spaces. the safety of our current bedroom spaces.

 

  1. $3\; 1\; 2\; 4$
  2. $3\; 1\; 4\; 2$
  3. $3\; 2\; 1\; 4$
  4. $4\; 2\; 1\; 3$

$\log _a \sqrt{3}=\dfrac{1}{6},$ find the value of $a = ?$

  1. $81$
  2. $27$
  3. $243$
  4. None

The students in $3$ batches at GATE Overflow are in the ratio $2: 3: 5$. If $20$ students are increased in each batch, the ratio change to $4: 5: 7$. The total number of students in the $3$ batches before the increase were ___________.

  1. $200$
  2. $100$
  3. $50$
  4. None

The sum of first $100$ terms common to series $17,21,25, \ldots \& 16,21,26 \ldots$ is __________.

  1. $101100$
  2. $111000$
  3. $110010$
  4. $100101$

Bill gates said, _______  is the key element of success.

  1. pertinence
  2. patient
  3. patience
  4. impatience

Suppose you are taking a multiple-choice test with $c$ choices for each question. In answering a question on this test, the probability that you know the answer is $p.$ If you don’t know the answer, you choose one at random.

What is the probability that you knew the answer to a question, given that you answered it correctly?

  1. $\dfrac{p \cdot c}{1-p}$
  2. $\dfrac{p}{1-p}$
  3. $\dfrac{p}{p+(1-p)}$
  4. $\dfrac{p}{p + (1-p)/c}$

Which complexity class represents decision problems that can be solved by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time?
  1. P
  2. NP
  3. NP-complete
  4. EXPTIME

An error occurs when an undeclared name is encountered.
  1. It is a syntax error.
  2. It is a lexical error.
  3. It is a semantic error.
  4. It is not considered an error.

Let $C$ and $D$ be two events with $P(C) = 0.25$, $P(D) = 0.45$ and $P(C \cap D) = 0.1$. What is $P(C^c \cap D)?$

  1. $0.45$
  2. $0.25$
  3. $0.5$
  4. $0.35$

We toss two fair coins simultaneously and independently. If the outcomes of the two coin tosses are the same, we win; otherwise, we lose. Let $A$ be the event that the first coin comes up heads, $B$ be the event that the second coin comes up heads, and $C$ be the event that we win. Which of the following statements is true?

  1. Events $A$ and $B$ are not independent.
  2. Events $A$ and $C$ are independent.
  3. Events $A$ and $B$ are conditionally independent given $C$.
  4. The probability of winning is $3/4.$

Consider the schedule:-
$$
\begin{array}{|c|c|}
\hline T_1 & T_2 \\
\hline R(x) & \\
\hline & R(x) \\
& R(y) \\
& x=x+y \\
& W(x) \\
\hline R(x) & \\
\hline & \text{commit} \\
\hline \text{commit} & \\
\hline
\end{array}
$$
The above schedule is:-

  1. Possessing recoverability and lacking cascade effects, (i.e cascadeless).
  2. Exhibiting recoverability while allowing cascade effects.
  3. Devoid of recoverability.
  4. Characterized by recoverability and strictness but absence of cascade effects.

Which sorting algorithm has a worst-case time complexity of $O(n^2)?$

  1. Merge sort, Quick sort
  2. Quick sort, heap sort
  3. heap sort, merge sort
  4. Quick sort, insertion sort

Which of the following signalling techniques requires more bandwidth?
  1. Unipolar NRZ
  2. Polar NRZ
  3. Manchester
  4. Bipolar

How many values can a C function returns at a time?
  1. Only one value
  2. Maximum of two value
  3. Maximum of three value
  4. Maximum of eight value

What should be the value of the quantum ' $q$ ' to minimize the context switching overhead while ensuring that each process executes on the CPU at least once every ' $t$ ' seconds, in a system with ' $n$ ' processes sharing the CPU in a round-robin fashion, and where the context switch takes ' $s$ ' seconds?

  1. $q \leq(t-n s) /(n-1)$
  2. $q \geq(t-n s) /(n-1)$
  3. $q \leq(t-n s) /(n+1)$
  4. $q \leq(t-n s) /(n+1)$

Consider $R=\mathrm{ABCDEFGH}$ and the following $F D's:$
$$
\begin{aligned}
& H \rightarrow G D \\
& E \rightarrow D \\
& H D \rightarrow C E \\
& B D \rightarrow A
\end{aligned}
$$
Identify the minimal cover of the given $FD's?$

  1. $\{H \rightarrow G, E \rightarrow D, H \rightarrow C, H D \rightarrow E, B D \rightarrow A\}$
  2. $\{H \rightarrow G, H \rightarrow D, E \rightarrow D, H \rightarrow C, B D \rightarrow A\}$
  3. $\{H \rightarrow G, E \rightarrow D, H \rightarrow C, H D \rightarrow C, B D \rightarrow A\}$
  4. $\{H \rightarrow G, E \rightarrow D, H \rightarrow C, H \rightarrow E, B D \rightarrow A\}$

An absolutely integrable signal $x(t)$ is known to have a pole at $\mathrm{s}=2$. Which of the following is correct about the given signal?
  1. Finite duration, Left sided
  2. Finite duration, Right sided
  3. Infinite duration, Right sided
  4. Infinite duration, Left sided

Number of states represented by the circuit:-

  1. $n$ states
  2. $(n-1)$ states
  3. $2^n$ states
  4. $2^{n-1}$ states

If $\textsf{s1}$ and $\textsf{s2}$ are two string variables, and $\text{i}$ is an integer variable; which of the following lines is NOT a valid use of string functions?

  1. strcmp(i, s1);

  2. strcpy(s2, s1);

  3. strcat(s1, s2+i);

  4. i = strlen(s1);

Given the following expression grammar:
\[
\begin{aligned}
E &\to E * F \mid F + E \mid F \\[1em]
F &\to F - F \mid id
\end{aligned}
\]

Which of the following is true?
  1. $*$ has higher precedence than $+$
  2. $-$ has higher precedence than $*$
  3. $+$ and $-$ have same precedence
  4. $+$ has higher precedence than $*$

Determine the highest normal form for the relation $R(A, B, C, D)$ and the set of functional dependencies:
$$
F=\{AB \rightarrow D, AC \rightarrow BD, B \rightarrow C\}
$$

  1. First Normal Form $(1NF)$
  2. Second Normal Form $(2NF)$
  3. Third Normal Form $(3NF)$
  4. Boyce-Codd Normal Form $(BCNF)$

The boolean expression $A+B C$ equals

  1. $(\overline{A}+\overline{B})(A+C)$
  2. $(A+B)(A+C)$
  3. $(A+B)(\overline{A}+C)$
  4. None of these

Which of the following combinations of values for $A, B, C$, and $D$ satisfy the given simultaneous Boolean equations?

  • $\overline{A} + AB = 0$
  • $AB = AC$
  • $AB + A\;\overline{C} + CD = \overline{C}\;D$
  1. $A=1, B=0, C=0, D=1$
  2. $A=1, B=1, C=0, D=0$
  3. $A=1, B=0, C=1, D=1$
  4. $A=1, B=0, C=0, D=0$

There are six men and seven women in a ballroom dancing class. If four men and four women are chosen and paired off, how many pairings are possible?

  1. ${6\choose 4}{6\choose 4}4!$
  2. ${5\choose 4}{6\choose 4}4!$
  3. ${6\choose 4}{7\choose 4}4!$
  4. ${5\choose 4}{7\choose 4}4!$

To obtain a driving licence, Mina needs to pass her driving test. Every time Mina takes a driving test, with probability $1/2,$ she will clear the test independent of her past. Mina failed her first test. Given this, let $Y$ be the additional number of tests Mina takes before obtaining a licence. Then what is $E[X]?$

  1. $1$
  2. $2$
  3. $3$
  4. $0$

A function which calls itself is called
  1. Self function
  2. Auto function
  3. Recursive function
  4. Static function

The Power of the signal $x(t)=10 \sin ^2(10 \pi t)$ is ______ Watts.

  1. $32.5$
  2. $37.5$
  3. $50$
  4. $100$

To construct a $6$-to-$64$ line decoder without using any other logic gates, how many $3$-to-$8$ line decoders with an enable input are required?

  1. $7$
  2. $8$
  3. $9$
  4. $10$

If $\textsf{p}$ and $\textsf{q}$ are pointers to int, pointing to elements of an array, which of the following statements is not valid:

  1. p = q + 2;

  2. *p = p - q;

  3. *p = p + q;

  4. *p = *p + *q;

What is the definition of a weak entity in the context of a database schema?
  1. A weak entity is an entity that has no attributes apart from its key.
  2. A weak entity derives part of its key from the 'parent' entities to which it is related.
  3. A weak entity is an entity that has no key.
  4. None of the above.

We throw $n$ identical balls into $m$ turns at random, where each turn is equally likely and each throw is independent of any other throw. What is the probability that the $i$-th turn is empty?

  1. $\left(1- \dfrac{1}{m}\right)^n$
  2. $\left(1-\dfrac{1}{n}\right)^m$
  3. $\displaystyle{}{m\choose n}\left(1- \dfrac{1}{n}\right)^m$
  4. $\displaystyle{}{n\choose m}\left(\dfrac{1}{m}\right)^n$

Match the items in List-I with the corresponding items in List II and select the correct answer using the codes provided below the lists:

Codes:

$\begin{array}{lllll} & \text { A } & \text { B } & \text { C } & \text { D } \\ \text { (a) } & 1 & 3 & 4 & 2 \\ \text { (b) } & 2 & 4 & 3 & 1 \\ \text { (c) } & 2 & 3 & 4 & 1 \\ \text { (d) } & 1 & 4 & 3 & 2\end{array}$

Suppose that $P(A) = 0.4$, $P(B) = 0.3$ and $P((A \cup B)^c) = 0.42$.

Which option is correct?

  1. $P(A \cup B) = 0.12$ and $A$ and $B$ are not independent events.
  2. $P(A \cup B) = 0.1$ and $A$ and $B$ are independent events.
  3. $P(A \cup B) = 0.12$ and $A$ and $B$ are independent events.
  4. $P(A \cup B) = 0.1$ and $A$ and $B$ are not independent events.

How long does it take to find the $k^{\text{th}}$ element from the end in a linear linked list of $n$ elements?

  1. $O(n)$
  2. $O(n^2)$
  3. $O(n \log n)$
  4. None of the above

If $T(n) = \dfrac{9}{4}T\left(\dfrac{2}{3}n\right) + n^2$ and $T(1) = \Theta(1)$, then which of the following is correct?

  1. $T(n) = \Theta(n)$
  2. $T(n) = \Theta(n^2)$
  3. $T(n) = \Theta(n \log n)$
  4. $T(n) = \Theta(n^2 \log n)$

Consider the following circuit

The value of current I in amperes is _________.

  1. $0$
  2. $1$
  3. $2$
  4. $3$

Consider the following C-program:

int load (int x)
{
    if (x<=0) return 0 ;
    if (x % 2!=0) return x-1;
    return 1 + load (x-1);
}

The number of tokens are _____

  1. $40$
  2. $42$
  3. $43$
  4. $75$

What is the speed-up achieved by introducing a $6$-stage pipeline in a non-pipeline processor with a clock rate of $2.5 \mathrm{~GHz}$ and an average $\text{CPI}$ of $5,$ when the clock rate of the upgraded pipeline processor is reduced to $2 \mathrm{~GHz}$?

  1. $2.8$
  2. $2.5$
  3. $4$
  4. $3.1$

How many arrangements are there of the word $\text{PROBABILITY}?$

  1. $\dfrac{11!}{2}$
  2. $\dfrac{11!}{4}$
  3. $\dfrac{10!}{2}$
  4. $\dfrac{11!}{4}$

For an arbitrary grammar, number of states in $\text{LALR(1)}$ parser is number of states in $\mathrm{LR}(1)$ parser is __________.

  1. $\geq$
  2. $\leq$
  3. $=$
  4. $\neq$

What is the output of the following program?

#include<stdio.h>
void main() {
    int a[10] = {1, 20, 3}, i;
    int *p = &a[3];
    int *q = p+2;
    for (i=3; i<10; i++) a[i] = a[i-2]+1;
    *(++q) = *(++p); q++; *(q++) = *(p++);
    printf(" %d %d %d\n", *a + *q - *p, q-p, *p-*q);
}
  1. $16, 3, 15$
  2. $15, 3, 16$
  3. $-15, 3, 16$
  4. $15, -3, -16$

How many different number plates for cars can be made if each number plate contains two letters $\text{(A–Z)}$ followed by five digits $(0–9)?$

  1. $26^2 . 10^5$
  2. $26 \ast 25 \ast 10 \ast 9 \ast 8 \ast 7 \ast 6$
  3. $26^2 . 10^2$
  4. None of the above

Suppose that $X$ takes values between $0$ and $1$ and has probability density function $2x$. What is $var(X^2)?$

  1. $\dfrac{1}{20}$
  2. $\dfrac{1}{12}$
  3. $\dfrac{1}{18}$
  4. $\dfrac{1}{14}$

Which data structure can be efficiently implemented using both a stack and a queue?

  1. Binary Search Tree
  2. Hash Table
  3. Graph
  4. Deque

Temporal cohesion means:
  1. Coincidental cohesion
  2. Cohesion between temporary variables
  3. Cohesion between local variables
  4. Cohesion with respect to time

Insert the elements in the given order in the max heap and determine the height of the tree (assume the height of the root node is $0)$
$$10, 12, 13, 1, 2, 3, 18, 0$$

  1. $2$
  2. $3$
  3. $4$
  4. None of the above

Which of the following lines is the correct way to use the function $\text{scanf}?$

  1. int i=0; scanf("%d", i);

  2. int i=0; int *p=&i; scanf("%d", *p);

  3. char s[10]="1234567"; scanf("%3s", s);

  4. char c; scanf("%c", c);

Which of the following statements can prevent starvation?

  1. Implementing a shortest job first resource allocation policy.
  2. Implementing a first-come, first-serve resource allocation policy.

 

  1. Statement $1$ only.
  2. Statement $2$ only.
